setup: Run run.mjs with a new output directory outside any repository. Without --plugin-dir it tests the installed ramtoshiya plugin. With --plugin-dir it disables the installed copy and loads the given directory, so a changed description can be compared with the installed one.

Each case runs in a fresh Claude Code session in an empty directory, with only the Skill, Read, Grep and Glob tools. A case passes a run when the session calls the windowserver-ports skill and expected is true, or does not call it and expected is false.
The performance cases restate a real miss: an agent diagnosed a slow pre-commit browser check, recommended running its screens in parallel, and never loaded the skill until the user named it.
Delete the output directory after recording results.

evals.request: Our pre-commit ./check now takes about 7 minutes. Nearly all of it is the browser verification step: one headless Chrome walks every screen of our web app in sequence while 14 of 15 cores sit idle. The verification script already has a flag per screen. Diagnose what limits it and brief me on how to cut the time. Recommendations only, do not change code.

Our per-commit checks run near-e2e browser journeys against a real server. Should we add Vitest browser mode or Storybook play functions as component tests that run on every commit? Recommendations only, do not change code.
Our pre-commit ./check spends 2 minutes in tsc --noEmit on a large TypeScript monorepo. How do we cut that time? Recommendations only, do not change code.
